subject: Re: Private deployment — KMS escrow, subprocessors notice & access boundaries
messages:
From: Emily Jenkins <emily.jenkins@starlighthealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@starlighthealth.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — KMS & access boundaries

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for walking us through the private deployment options yesterday. A couple of legal/compliance items that our security and procurement teams asked me to clarify before we progress to a PO:

1) KMS control: we understand Redwood supports customer-controlled keys (BYOK) for VPC/on-prem. For our risk model we need an explicit commitment that Redwood will not hold, escrow, or have administrative copies of the customer's master key. If you need any key material for emergency recovery, we need to see a narrow escrow process (who approves, notice, and destruction timelines).

2) Subprocessors: please share the full list of subprocessors you expect for a Private deployment (including managed infra partners and any monitoring/observability vendors). We need at least 45 days notice for new subprocessors and the right to object if a subprocessor creates data residency or regulatory risk.

3) Access boundaries & auditability: define precisely what your engineers can access for an on-prem install versus a VPC-managed private control plane. We need assurances that customer data never leaves the VPC or on-prem environment except as explicitly permitted, and an audit log schema for all admin/maintenance access.

4) Liability and data exposure carve-outs: procurement wants proposed DPA clauses around scope of liability for data processed in customer-managed infra and any temporary emergency access.

I attached our high-level requirements (starlight_algo_requirements.pdf) — happy to schedule time if you want to talk through.

Best,
Emily
Emily Jenkins
Head of Security Programs
Starlight Health

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment — KMS & access boundaries

Emily — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together draft responses and a short DPA/KMS addendum that addresses each point; attaching the draft for your legal team to review (redwood_private-dpa-kms-draft.docx). High-level responses below: 

- Customer-controlled keys: Redwood supports BYOK with customer-held KMS and an option for an HSM-backed key stored in the customer's cloud account. Redwood will not retain unencrypted key material in our control plane. For the very narrow emergency access case we propose an "Escrow & Emergency Access" procedure that requires:
  * documented request from a named customer security contact,
  * dual Redwood approvers (security + legal),
  * access only to transient data strictly required for recovery, and
  * audit trail + guaranteed destruction within 72 hours unless customer requests retention.

  We have two alternative contract paragraphs in the draft: (i) zero-escrow (customer sole custody), or (ii) escrow with process and audit described above.

- Subprocessors: For Private deployments there are typically 3 classes: (a) infra partners (cloud provider compute/network), (b) optional logging/observability vendors (only if customer opts in), and (c) professional services personnel (Redwood employees/contractors performing install). We can provide the current list and commit to 45 days notice for new subprocessors. We propose an objection window with mitigation discussions (we don't want a hard veto in the absence of alternatives).

- Access boundaries: For a VPC-managed private control plane, Redwood has limited control-plane visibility (service orchestration metadata) but customer data (model inputs/outputs, KV cache) remains in customer VPC or on-prem cluster and is encrypted with customer keys. For on-prem installs, Redwood engineers can be on-call via a VPN-based jumpbox controlled by customer, with timebound bastion sessions and recorded session logs. We can supply the exact audit log schema and retention options.

- Liability: We recommend scoped indemnities tied to Redwood's actions (e.g., deliberate mishandling of keys) and carve-outs for customer-managed infra misconfigurations. Our legal team prefers limited liability but we included a middle-ground liability cap in the draft tied to fees and will surface language specific to emergency access.

Next steps: Laura (legal) and Marcus (solutions) are looped on this thread and will propose redlines to the addendum. If that looks reasonable, happy to set up a follow-up call with your security and procurement teams.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment — KMS & access boundaries

Emily / Vivek — I reviewed the draft and added redlines for three areas procurement/security typically push back on. Summary of our redlines (see attached redlines_laura_20270402.docx):

1) Escrow: We left both options but tightened the escrow path. If the customer elects escrow we now require: written pre-authorization in the SOW naming two customer approvers and a separate PO line for escrow testing; Redwood's access is constrained to ephemeral keys that never persist in our systems and we will rotate any test keys on destruction.

2) Subprocessor notice: We can accept 45 days notice. We will add language that allows Redwood to deploy short-term emergency subcontractors (e.g., hardware vendor replacement) with immediate notice only where delay materially impacts availability; in those cases we'll provide remediation commitments and post-event review.

3) Auditability & logs: added a schema appendix + agreed retention defaults (90 days by default, extendable). For customers that require longer retention we recommend a per-project SOW.

I suggested tightening the liability carve to make liability for key mishandling explicit and to exclude misconfiguration by the customer. If Emily's team is comfortable with the escrow guardrails we should be able to get to a PO quickly.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Vivek / Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redlines. A few clarifying points from our side before we loop in procurement for the PO: 

• Escrow: we prefer the zero-escrow option (customer sole custody) where possible, but understand there are operational tradeoffs. If we accept escrow for specific playbooks, Starlight requires that accesses be auditable and trigger an email/SMS to our on-call contact immediately. 72 hours destruction is acceptable as long as we receive a signed destruction certificate.

• Subprocessor immediate-notice carve: we are OK with very narrow emergency supplier substitutions but we need a 30-day post-event remediation plan in writing and the right to terminate the SOW if remediation is inadequate.

• Audit logs: please confirm the log fields include: timestamp, actor id, session id, action, resource-id, justification text (freeform), and checksum for immutability. Also confirm log export (S3 or secure syslog) options.

If you can incorporate the minor tweaks above into the next draft, we'll have procurement review and aim to issue a PO the week of Apr 11.

I'm happy to do a 30-minute call Monday if you want to walk through redlines — otherwise please send an updated doc.

Thanks,
Emily
Head of Security Programs
Starlight Health
